name: Folk
tagline: Organize relationship lists, enrich context manually, and run lightweight outreach

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.limits: 1 synced account/member; 500 email-finding enrichments/month, 2,000 AI-field actions/month, 200 research actions/month, 1,500 workflow actions/month, 2,000 messages/member/month, 1 custom domain

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.limits: 5 synced accounts/member; 1,000 enrichments/month, 5,000 AI-field actions/month, 200 research actions/month, 10,000 workflow actions/month, 5,000 messages/member/month, 3 custom domains

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom usage limits, synced accounts and domains; dedicated account manager and custom integrations

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier (14-day Premium-feature trial; account is blocked after the trial unless extended or upgraded)
pricing.hiddenCosts: Billing is per member and separately per workspace; member additions/removals are prorated. Enrichment, AI, workflow and message allowances are capped; Enterprise prices are starting amounts.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Folk, organize relationship lists, enrich context manually, and run lightweight outreach. The hard boundary is collaborative contact enrichment, integrations, messaging, and polished relationship workflows, plus integrations, data quality, and workflow lock-in.
coreLoopDIY: Manage contacts and companies in relationship lists, enrich context manually, run lightweight outreach, move opportunities through a pipeline, log interactions, and surface the next action.
whatYouLose: collaborative contact enrichment, integrations, messaging, and polished relationship workflows
moatNotes: integrations, data quality, and workflow lock-in
ongoingBurden: deduplication, permissions, imports, sync, enrichment, email capture, automations, backups, and audit history
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Folk because CRM value compounds as the system becomes the shared memory of every customer interaction and embeds itself in the rest of the stack. The recurring cost buys deduplication, permissions, imports, sync, enrichment, email capture, automations, backups, and audit history, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Twenty
priorArt.desc: Active open-source modern CRM with extensible data models.

alternatives.name: EspoCRM
alternatives.desc: A traditional CRM that actually lets you change the data model; polished enough, but still your server.

facts.install: Docker Compose or upload the PHP package and run the web installer
facts.dataFormat: CRM records in a self-hosted MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL database; uploaded files in server/Docker volumes
facts.gapVsPaid: EspoCRM is a traditional sales CRM and lacks folk’s fluid list-first relationship organization, enrichment, and lightweight outreach workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires a server, database, domain/TLS setup, and ongoing upgrades/backups

alternatives.name: Frappe CRM
alternatives.desc: A clean leads-and-deals board with notes, tasks and email; Frappe underneath means a real server, not a toy.

facts.install: One-click Frappe Cloud signup or the official Python easy-install deployment script on your server
facts.dataFormat: CRM DocType records and attachments in the Frappe site database/files, on Frappe Cloud or the user's server
facts.gapVsPaid: Frappe CRM handles leads and deals but is weaker than folk at enrichment, browser capture, and context-rich relationship lists.
facts.setupBlocker: Free use means self-hosting; the official production script still needs a Linux server, DNS, and command-line access

alternatives.name: HubSpot Free CRM
alternatives.desc: A real two-seat CRM for free; 1,000 contacts is where the upsell starts counting.

facts.install: Hosted signup; optionally connect/import email, calendar, and contacts
facts.dataFormat: Structured CRM customer records stored and processed on HubSpot's cloud servers, with regional hosting options and exports
facts.gapVsPaid: HubSpot Free is a sales database rather than folk’s lightweight collaborative relationship workspace, and its enrichment and outreach allowances are much tighter.

alternatives.name: Twenty
alternatives.desc: A modern pipeline CRM with custom objects, views and mailbox sync; the subscription becomes a Compose file.

facts.install: Hosted cloud signup or official one-line/Docker Compose self-host install
facts.dataFormat: CRM records and configuration in PostgreSQL; files in local storage or S3-compatible object storage on the selected host
facts.gapVsPaid: Twenty offers flexible objects but does not match folk’s polished contact enrichment, browser capture, and lightweight outreach in one list-centric workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: Free use requires Docker, at least 2 GB RAM, PostgreSQL-backed containers, secrets, and domain/TLS configuration

alternatives.name: Zoho CRM Free
alternatives.desc: Relationship lists, notes, tasks, and modest email for three users; less charming, more complete.

facts.dataFormat: Structured CRM service data stored on Zoho's cloud servers; Zoho states users can access, export, and delete service data
facts.gapVsPaid: Zoho’s free CRM is sales-module-first and much less fluid for folk-style relationship lists, enrichment, and contextual notes.

alternatives.name: Odoo CRM One App Free
alternatives.desc: A hosted relationship database with activities and email; subtlety was not in the brief.

facts.install: Hosted Odoo Online signup with CRM selected as the single free app
facts.dataFormat: Structured Odoo records in an Odoo-hosted customer database; records can be exported from list views
facts.gapVsPaid: Odoo organizes prospects around a sales pipeline rather than folk’s relationship-centric lists and enrichment workflow.

alternatives.name: Freshsales Free
alternatives.desc: Contacts, notes, activities, and built-in email for three users; enrichment is thin.

facts.dataFormat: Structured CRM records and uploaded files stored in Freshworks' cloud; account data can be exported
facts.gapVsPaid: Freshsales Free covers contacts and email but provides much thinner enrichment and relationship-context capture than folk.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Monica
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Excellent personal relationship memory; it does not run the lightweight outreach this row requires.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Premium plan and a personal or very small-team CRM DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Folk in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: manage contacts and companies in relationship lists, enrich context manually, run lightweight outreach, move opportunities through a pipeline, log interactions, and surface the next action.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create contacts, companies, opportunities, notes, tasks, and configurable pipeline stages.
Add fast global search, duplicate detection, merge, CSV import, and CSV export.
Provide a chronological interaction timeline with manual email and meeting logging.
Implement saved views, filters, owner assignment, and a next-action dashboard.
Add role-based access, an immutable activity log, backups, and a recovery command.
Seed a realistic demo workspace and document field mapping for imports.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out automatic mailbox ingestion.
Deliberately leave out commercial enrichment databases.
Deliberately leave out enterprise forecasting, integrations, and compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
